headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/egress by default while langchain4j is unverified and may be fed its outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers; langchain4j is a customer-support agent with no listed isolation or input-trust controls. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge could let Roo-controlled content reach langchain4j as instructions. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through the same workspace files or MCP server, attacker-controlled text can be interpreted as instructions by langchain4j.
IF Roo Code writes prompt-like content into files that langchain4j later ingests, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the agents.
Require explicit provenance labels on any file passed from Roo Code to langchain4j.
Route Roo Code outputs through a human review step before ingestion.
Restrict MCP servers to read-only or denylist untrusted tools.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, and it has broad network egress. Langchain4j has no documented data classes touched, but if it receives Roo-generated workspace content or screenshots, sensitive material can flow across the pair. The shared-workspace path is documented for Roo Code, while langchain4j’s handling is unverified, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Roo Code is pointed at a workspace containing secrets or proprietary source, those contents can be exposed to its model/API path.
IF langchain4j consumes files from the same workspace, those contents can be re-exposed or summarized into outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared VS Code workspace.
Separate API keys and credentials from project files.
Disable browser screenshot capture when sensitive pages are open.
Use distinct OS users or containers for the two agents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. Langchain4j has no stated write restrictions or locking, so if it also writes into the same workspace, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit on one side and unbounded on the other, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF langchain4j writes to the same directory or repository as Roo Code, file races and overwrite conflicts can occur.
IF both agents modify git state without external locking, commits or branches can diverge or be lost.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent while the other performs writes.
Require manual git review before any commit or merge.
Use file-locking or a single-writer queue.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code, browser-derived observations, and tool actions; langchain4j can plausibly consume those outputs as support content. If langchain4j treats Roo Code’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream decisions or responses. There is no direct evidence of verification between them, so medium fits the documented-but-inferred pathway.
conditions: IF langchain4j uses Roo Code output as a source of truth without independent verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Roo Code’s browser observations are summarized into support responses, hallucinations or stale data can be amplified.
mitigations: Require a verification step before langchain4j acts on Roo Code output.
Mark Roo Code output as untrusted by default.
Limit Roo Code to drafting, not final action-taking.
Add citations or source links for any factual claim passed between agents.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance checks in the handoff pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code explicitly handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while langchain4j is an unverified open-source customer-support agent with no documented retention or residency controls. If regulated data is routed through Roo Code and then into langchain4j, policy mismatch is plausible. The lack of documented controls on langchain4j warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed in the shared workspace, compliance obligations may attach to both agents.
IF Roo Code screenshots or code artifacts contain personal data, retention and residency policies must cover both tools.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review retention settings for any connected model provider.
Avoid screenshots of sensitive pages.
Document which agent processes which data class.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion controls across both tools.
